thought.text: GDAL is at 26% with 8 parallel jobs. This will take several minutes. Polling periodically.

reasoning_content:
Build is at 26%, running (35 processes). GDAL is a large build and could take 10-20 minutes with -j8. Wait and poll periodically. Meanwhile, could I set up the poetry venv in the meantime? Actually, poetry install is already partially done (everything except gdal was installed into the venv? No—poetry install failed on gdal, so the remaining packages that come alphabetically after gdal (geojson, geopandas, pillow, pyarrow, pypdf, python-magic, rdflib, ruff... wait, did those show up as "Installing" in the log before the gdal failure? Let me recheck: in the log, after the gdal line, geojson, geopandas, pillow, pyarrow, pypdf, python-magic, rdflib, ruff are listed. Those "- Installing" lines appear to be printed as the install starts for each package. Actually, in poetry's output, each line is printed when the install starts, and the failure occurred at gdal. The lines after gdal might just have been pre-scheduled... hmm, actually poetry 2.x lists out all pending packages first, and then processes them in order. The error occurred after "Installing ruff" was printed... the tail shows:

```
  - Installing coverage (7.9.2)
  - Installing fiona (1.10.1)
  - Installing frictionless (5.18.1)
  - Installing gdal (3.6.2)
  - Installing geojson (3.2.0)
  - Installing geopandas (1.1.1)
  - Installing pillow (11.3.0)
  - Installing pyarrow (18.1.0)
  - Installing pypdf (5.7.0)
  - Installing python-magic (0.4.27)
  - Installing rdflib (7.1.4)
  - Installing ruff (0.6.9)
```

Followed by PEP517 build failure. Poetry prints all the install operations first, then executes. So the state of the venv is partial. Once gdal starts succeeding, re-running `poetry install` will resume from the lockfile and install the rest.

Wait for the GDAL build. Poll roughly every 90 seconds. Total build time on 8 cores is probably 10-15 minutes.
